title: The Crown of Precious Stones
english: The hypothesis of the psalm is taken, and it is spoken regarding the human economy. Perhaps it is also for all those believing, fulfilling the body of Christ according to the teaching that not even Christ is one body, but many members; Christ is said to be saved, and those who have become his body and members may have salvation (1 Cor 12:27). And also to say 'Now I know'—for 'now' means in this present age we know Christ is saving, receiving the earnest of salvation from hereafter.

He hearkens to Christ according to every foretold repayment. And the right hand of God, that is, his Word, makes salvation, not by chance, but with power, like a best general or king. Regarding Ps 19:8, thinking of horses, the skittish powers of passions that ride upon them; and chariots, the concord of the rushing passions prepared against us. But even if not in these things, the unvanquishable defense of us is the approach of God. Regarding Ps 20:2–3, the one established as king upon Zion is truly and certainly king, rejoicing in divine joy from the power of God present to him. And let the whole psalm be interpreted concerning Christ the king and the one co-reigning with him, so that we are not compelled to signify this for every single word.

He does not fulfill the desire of the flesh, but walks by the Spirit (Gal 5:16). One strengthened by the Spirit receives the desire of the heart from God. For he, having abstained from the cravings of the flesh, hungers—that is, the mind hungers—and receives from God, who implants his desire in good things. But even if someone happens to be in need, he was not denied by the Lord because of the prayer of his lips. Regarding Ps 20:4–5, from 'Because you have preceded him in blessings of goodness'—by the causal connection of 'Because,' having used [it], he showed what rejoices and exults in having been preceded in blessings of goodness. And regarding the contrast of blessings, not of goodness...

Here, goodness is set forth; for Jacob, in blessing the sons, will answer the sons in a manner of blessing who have some toil, as their anger is the accursed one. And if such a thing is to be lacking, God foretells a king and his imitator in blessings of goodness, lifting them up to the supra-cosmic promises, which are sent to be a pledge.

One is crowned from his own works and practices. Without doubt, he who has justly pursued the just shall receive the crown of righteousness (2 Tim 4:8), and he who has rightly glorified the Trinity shall bring the incorruptible crown of glory (1 Pet 5:4). And one having been satisfied by the Lord's crown of luxury protects himself, and he being saved by grace receives a crown of graces for his own head.

But also he who has treasured precious stones with gold and silver, from which he worked precious stones, shall be crowned, God restoring to him the head of the soul with the crown of precious stones; and being adorned with divine power in every virtue, he is called, 'All a good stone you have bound.' God crowns not in mercy, but will crown with precious stones a crown made of them, as also in hope he crowns those watching for it; for the Lord Sabaoth is the crown of hope, spread with glory (Isa 66:14).

And since the apostle writes to his own disciples, 'Joy and my crown' (Phil 4:1), perhaps also those who are known to Christ, being precious stones through virtuous character, having placed a crown, will be set upon the head of Christ, as Paul says to the disciples, 'Joy and my crown' (Philem 1:21). He asked life from you and you gave it to him. If the imitator of Christ is the one concerning whom the Word is, God has given eternal life to him who asked life from him; for the gift of God is eternal life (John 6:40). But if he speaks concerning Christ, regarding the one who asked life from him, the Father gave, so that he might vivify the dead (Eph 2:5). Length of days unto the age of ages; toward the life...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
